transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, I suppose I'm here because... it's just gotten completely out of hand. I basically plan my whole entire summer around avoiding wasps. Which is a real shame, because summer used to be my favorite time of year. I actually had to give up my garden jobs at the church over it. 

The church garden used to be my pride and joy, you know. Pastor Dave put in these hydrangeas last year, and I told him, I said, the soil by the south wall is way too acidic if you want them to stay pink, and sure enough, they turned this awful muddy purple color. Just terrible. But I can't even go fix it now. I just can't be out there. 

It's the same at the house, really. If I so much as hear a buzzing sound, I'm done. I go straight inside and make my husband unload everything by the back porch. He grumbles about it, of course, says his knees aren't what they used to be since he stopped working, and I know grocery bags can be heavy, but I just... I can't be out there if there's a buzzing. So I make him do it.
Are there other situations or things that make you feel anxious, or is it specifically the presence of wasps and buzzing sounds that cause this reaction?

No, it's really just them. I mean, I'm not a fearful person generally. Spiders don't bother me, and I'm certainly not scared of mice or anything like that. Actually, last winter, my husband left the garage door cracked and a little field mouse got right into our pantry. Chewed through a brand new bag of flour. Flour was absolutely everywhere! It took me three days to get it all out of the floor tile grout. But I just scooped the little guy up in a bucket and put him out in the woods behind the house. Didn't bother me a bit. 

But with the wasps... I mean, I know a wasp is just a little insect. I know most folks would just swat it away without a second thought. My neighbor, Betty, she swats them with a rolled-up magazine like it's nothing while we're sitting on her porch. She gets all the magazines, you know, the celebrity gossip ones, the cooking ones... she makes this rhubarb pie from one of those magazines that is just to die for, by the way. She uses extra butter in the crust. 

But anyway, if one of those wasps gets anywhere near me, it just... it feels like something terrible is about to happen. I can't even explain it, my heart just drops. So yes, it's really just the wasps and that awful buzzing.

latest_inference.note: The patient's fear is specifically and exclusively tied to wasps and buzzing sounds, which does not align with the more general 'unspecified' phobia categories. The specificity of the trigger supports a diagnosis of 'other specified phobia' rather than 'specific phobia, unspecified' or 'animal type phobia' (which applies to broader categories like dogs or spiders rather than a specific insect like wasps). Anxiety Disorder, Unspecified (F41.9) is ruled out because the patient has a clear, circumscribed trigger rather than generalized anxiety.
